data.hypothesis: Two independent AVX-512 minimum accumulators may shorten the first-pass dependency chain compared with the fastest single-accumulator candidate, while avoiding the extra state of four accumulators. Retaining the ordered four-vector equality search preserves earliest-index selection. The interaction and performance still require measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as evidence when choosing the first-pass accumulator count; the timings are aggregate and do not establish performance by input pattern.
memory_lessons.claim: The two-pass AVX-512 candidate 8d was valid and measured 4.3046e-7 seconds; candidate 301734 was also valid and measured 4.4913e-7 seconds. The proposed two-accumulator first pass tests an unmeasured intermediate design, not an established speedup.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check correctness and measure this integrated candidate on both random and decreasing inputs; compare against 8d without assuming an improvement.

data.notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed. The two accumulators cover complete vectors in pairs, with an optional remaining vector and scalar tail; the second pass checks matching vectors in index order. Prior measurements are development/search outcomes, not independent confirmation of this candidate.
transformations: Replace the single first-pass vector minimum with two independent signed AVX-512 minimum accumulators, processing complete vectors in pairs and any remaining vector in one accumulator.
Combine the vector accumulators, reduce the signed minimum, and include the scalar tail in the minimum calculation.
Retain the four-vector equality-search groups, inspect matches in increasing vector order, select the lowest matching lane, then handle leftover vectors and the scalar tail.
